info.title: Orbit API
info.description: Digital asset management: assets, metadata, taxonomy, access control and delivery.

post.summary: Emits a system.ping event through the outbox (Admin only); consumed by the worker

get.summary: The caller: DAM user, effective roles, groups, permissions and attributes
Every permission a role may hold
Value counts for the given index fields (comma-separated) across every asset the caller may read

post.summary: Record uses of assets (1-500 per call): console downloads, proof of play, portals, apps. Resending a clientEventId is a duplicate, not an error; assets that do not exist or cannot be read are rejected

get.summary: The asset's latest workflow as a timeline of steps and their tasks; instance is null when none ever applied
All folders, flat (path order) or nested with ?tree=true
A folder with its ancestors and the metadata it inherits

post.summary: Re-parent a folder; the paths of everything beneath it are rewritten

get.summary: Terms of a vocabulary, flat or nested with ?tree=true
Current schema version per asset type
The current schema, or a specific version with ?version=

put.summary: Save the fields; a change creates the next version and old assets stay valid

post.summary: Check metadata against a schema; invalid metadata is a 422 with field-level errors

get.summary: Starter packs: vocabularies, metadata schemas, folders and workflows

post.summary: Add a pack's content. Additive and repeatable: nothing existing is changed or removed

get.summary: Assets the caller may read (interim listing; search arrives in Step 1.7)

post.summary: Create an asset shell (draft). Metadata is validated against the type's schema

get.summary: Every stored version, newest first, with the technical metadata read at ingest

post.summary: Makes an old version current again by copying it into a new version; history is never rewritten

get.summary: What differs between two versions: size, mime, checksum and technical metadata

post.summary: Moves an asset along its lifecycle: submit, approve, reject, publish, withdraw, expire, archive, purge
Sets or clears when the asset should publish or expire itself; the scheduler acts once it reaches the matching status
Blocks (or unblocks) retention purge for this asset, regardless of its policy's schedule

get.summary: Renditions already made for the current version

post.summary: Signed, expiring URLs to renditions or one transform, served by the delivery origin / CDN
Signed thumbnail links for many assets at once, for a library/search grid

get.summary: Near-duplicate images by perceptual hash (?by=phash&maxDistance=8)

post.summary: Open a resumable multipart upload; returns presigned part URLs. File bytes go straight to storage
One draft asset and one upload per file, all sharing the batch metadata and tags. Failures are per file

get.summary: State of a transfer. While open it lists the parts storage already has, which is where to resume from

post.summary: Fresh short-lived URLs for specific parts
Assemble the parts. Returns 202; poll the upload for ready, duplicate or failed

delete.summary: Refused while the policy is still assigned to any asset

post.summary: Query, filters, facets, sort, highlight and similar_to over every asset the caller may read

get.summary: Title matches for typeahead
Every collection the caller owns, that is shared tenant-wide, or - for a curator - every one
A static collection's members, or a smart collection's saved search run now - both filtered to what the caller may read

post.summary: Static collections only

get.summary: Assets not used in the last N days (days, default 30) or since a date (before); never-used assets are judged from their creation date. Longest idle first. Needs analytics.read
Usage, top assets, uploads per week and storage for the dashboard. Needs analytics.read
Workflow definitions with how many folders and bindings use each and how many assets are running through it. Needs workflow.manage or folders.manage

post.summary: Create a workflow from a definition (version 1: steps, assignees, any/all, SLA, escalation, routing). An invalid definition is 422 with errors addressed by path
Checks a definition without saving it. Always 200: valid, or a list of errors addressed by path (for the designer's live feedback)

get.summary: Which workflow applies to assets of a type and/or region when no folder names a default

put.summary: Replaces the whole list of type/region bindings. Needs workflow.manage
Replaces a workflow. Assets already going through it keep the definition they started with

delete.summary: 409 while a folder uses it as default, a binding points at it, or an asset is running through it

get.summary: The task inbox: tasks the caller can decide (assignee=me, default) or has decided; assignee=all lists every task and needs workflow.manage. status=pending (default), decided or all
Counts for the caller's inbox, plus tenant totals and 30-day SLA attainment for workflow.manage / analytics.read holders (null for others)

post.summary: Approve or reject a task (a comment is required to reject). Needs to be an assignee, workflow.tasks.decide and assets.approve on the asset. 409 if already decided

get.summary: The caller's own notifications, newest first (unread=true for unread only; limit up to 200; cursor from nextCursor)
How many unread notifications the caller has (for the badge)

post.summary: Marks all of the caller's notifications read
Marks one of the caller's notifications read (404 for anyone else's)

get.summary: The notification categories with the caller's in-app and email settings (their own choice, else the default), and whether the server can send email

put.summary: Sets the caller's settings for the categories listed; others keep theirs

get.summary: Slack and Teams channels that receive messages for matching events. Needs notifications.manage

post.summary: Adds a chat channel. The incoming-webhook URL is stored encrypted and never returned

put.summary: Replaces a channel's settings; a null url keeps the stored one

post.summary: Posts a test message to the channel and reports what the chat service answered

get.summary: The events webhooks and chat channels can subscribe to. Needs webhooks.manage or notifications.manage
Webhooks with their last-24-hour delivery counts. Needs webhooks.manage

post.summary: Creates a webhook. The signing secret is in this response only (whsec_...); keep it. Private and internal addresses are refused

put.summary: Replaces a webhook's name, URL, events and active flag (the secret is unchanged)

delete.summary: Deletes a webhook and its delivery history

post.summary: Generates a new signing secret, returned once; the old one stops working at once
Sends a synthetic webhook.ping event now and returns the delivery with its outcome (409 if the webhook is switched off)

get.summary: One webhook's deliveries, newest first. Filter by status (pending, succeeded, failed), eventType (exact, or a prefix such as workflow.*) and created time (from, to)
The delivery log across all webhooks (same filters as a single webhook's, plus webhookId)
One delivery with the exact payload sent and the receiver's response excerpt

post.summary: Creates a new delivery of the same payload (new id, replayOf set), attempts it now and returns it with its outcome

get.summary: Audit entries, newest first. Filters: from/to (time), actor (identity subject or Orbit user id), action (prefix, e.g. asset.), entityType, entityId, q (free text over action, entity and actor). limit up to 200; cursor from nextCursor
The distinct action names recorded, for a filter picker
Recomputes the hash chain over the rows in the time range (all of them when no range is given) and reports whether it is intact, or the first row that is not

Streams the filtered audit log as a file (format=csv or cef). It begins and ends with # comment lines stating whether the hash chain verified over the time range, the row count and the first and last hashes
